Account background: mid-market SaaS vendor (customer engagement platform) with ~500 employees; heavy chat/agent product used by 120+ customers. CTO (Maya Ruiz) frustrated with current LLM provider due to repeated latency regressions over last 3 months — causes live UX regressions and escalations from key customers. They prefer Redwood's unified hosted -> dedicated path: start on Hosted API for fast time-to-value, then commit to Dedicated if throughput/SLAs meet expectations.

POC summary: started Hosted API POC 2026-02-01. Goal: validate streaming latency SLO (95th and 99th tail), tool-calling reliability, and cost per 1k messages at production mix. Internal metric targets: 95th latency < 250ms for streaming tokens, 99th < 450ms; end-to-end tool call success > 99.5% under 200 RPS; cost sensitivity: target < $0.08 / 1k tokens averaged.

Benchmarking so far (notes from SE):
- IncumbentProviderX (baseline): observed median streaming token latency 60ms, 95th 340ms, 99th 720ms during peak test at 150 RPS; frequent jitter spikes correlated with background rollout on vendor side.
- Redwood Hosted (initial): median 55ms, 95th 180–210ms, 99th 320–360ms across same workload; streaming delivery more consistent, lower jitter. Tool-calling reliability: Redwood 99.8% successful websockets handoffs; incumbent 98.0% with intermittent timeouts.
- Notes: Redwood streaming shows tighter tail and more stable throughput in our synthetic tests. SE recommends next run with more realistic session length distribution and prefix cache enabled.

Quotes / call highlights:
- CTO Maya Ruiz: "We can't absorb 400–700ms tail latencies anymore — churn risk is real. Need deterministic streaming and a clear path to dedicated capacity."
- Head of Platform (Jared Kim): "If Redwood's Dedicated gives us consistent tail latency and a simple migration, procurement will push for a 12-month committed plan."

Procurement & security thread: Security team requested SOC2 Type II report, KMS integration details, and VPC peering guidance. Legal asked for sample SLA for Dedicated (latency SLA + credits) and data residency confirmation for EU customers.

Follow-up actions captured in CRM:

- Sales to deliver Dedicated pricing/commit tiers and attempted price decks comparing committed vs on-demand.
